San Jose, 1993. You're eating pancakes at Denny's. Next to you, three engineers draw chips on napkins.
Hey kid. We're starting a company. Want in? Just a hundred bucks.
More coffee, boys? You've been here four hours.
Two years later, their first chip flops. The money is almost gone.
Most games don't even work on it!
But the boss of Sega still invests five million dollars.
1999. NVIDIA hits the stock market. This time, you buy. A hundred dollars.
Then AI explodes. And it all runs on NVIDIA chips.
Today, your hundred dollars is worth about six hundred thousand.
